publication_finding: The 2019 KPHC publication describes population and household tables for county, sub-county and administrative units (county, sub-county, division, location and sub-location). It does not publish a direct table for the current 290 constituencies. KNBS's constituency table published in 2013 is based on the earlier census/boundary configuration and cannot be assigned to the current 2012-01 290-constituency registry without an authoritative crosswalk.
rules: Do not inherit a sub-county value into a constituency merely because a name overlaps.
Do not aggregate administrative units to constituencies without an authoritative 2019 administrative-unit to 2012-01 constituency crosswalk.
Do not remap the legacy pre-2012 KNBS constituency table to the current 290 constituencies.
A census questionnaire field recording constituency does not by itself constitute a published constituency statistic.
Refresh this closure if KNBS publishes a direct 290-constituency table or an authoritative crosswalk supporting deterministic aggregation.

decisions.source: KNBS — 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census Reports
decisions.reason: KNBS's 2019 KPHC publication does not publish population as a direct current-290-constituency table. Published county/sub-county/administrative-unit values are not inherited or cross-walked without an authoritative boundary mapping. P28A re-opened this closure on 2026-09-16 and independently re-verified and substantially extended the original finding rather than grandfathering it: (1) Volume II (Distribution of Population by Administrative Units) was downloaded and its full text inspected directly. Its own table of contents confirms its finest published tiers are Table 2.2 county, Table 2.3 sub-county, Table 2.4 sub-location and Table 2.5 urban centres; the word 'Constituency' occurs only twice in the ~250-page volume, as blank geocoding fields on the reproduced household questionnaire form in the appendix, not as a published statistic — this directly confirms rule 4 below rather than merely asserting it. (2) The separately-linked KNBS page above (legacy_constituency_table_url) was re-examined directly: it does list all 290 constituencies matching the current post-2012 delimitation, but it was published 2013-03-22 and its figures are the 2009 census count, not the 2019 KPHC — independently corroborated by the Humanitarian Data Exchange, which hosts the identical table explicitly titled 'Kenya population per constituency (2009).csv'. This sharpens the prior reason: the disqualifying defect is a census-period/vintage mismatch (2009 count presented as 2019 KPHC data), not solely a boundary mismatch. (3) Kenyan press reporting contemporaneous with the 2019 KPHC release (The Star, 2020-03-01, 'IEBC, KNBS battle over control of crucial data'; Daily Nation, 'Storm brewing over review of constituency boundaries') documents that KNBS compiled an unpublished internal 'Volume V' tabulating 2019 population by constituency and ward for the IEBC delimitation review, but withheld it from public release amid an unresolved inter-agency dispute over electoral-boundary shapefiles; a KNBS official is quoted: 'Unfortunately we cannot release the same without clear boundaries.' Reporters who sought the document directly were unable to obtain it. This Atlas has no access to an unpublished government working document and records this only as evidence that no publicly citable table exists, not as a promotion path. (4) As of 2025-2026 reporting the position has not improved: IEBC confirmed no constituency/ward boundary review will occur before the 2027 general election, citing among other reasons that 'KNBS has yet to clarify whether the 2019 census figures can be used as the legal basis for delimitation'; separately, the Garissa High Court (Petition No. 4 of 2020, Sheikh & 24 Others v KNBS, IEBC & 3 Others, ruling 2025-01-28) invalidated the 2019 KPHC count for Garissa, Wajir and Mandera counties (14 of 290 constituencies) and ordered a fresh census there, with the Court of Appeal (Civil Appeal No. 236 of 2025) since directing that matter remain in status quo pending determination of the appeal. Part of the underlying 2019 county-level count is therefore itself under active, unresolved judicial challenge, independent of the constituency-table publication gap. (5) The P28A secondary/modelled fallback hierarchy was searched exhaustively for a representation opportunity: no third-party aggregator (HDX, OCHA Kenya COD-AB/COD-PS, WorldPop's published country products, Wikipedia) hosts a 2019-vintage current-290-constituency population table; every constituency-level population dataset located, including on HDX, is the 2009 count. OCHA's Kenya COD-AB/COD-PS products stop at ADM2 (sub-county) and are documented as not reconciling to constituency geography. A genuinely modelled S5 fallback (aggregating a WorldPop-style gridded population raster to the Atlas's own existing 2012-01 constituency polygons in data/geography/geometry/constituencies.geojson) was considered, consistent with this programme's modelled-estimate allowance, but this repository currently has no raster/zonal-statistics tooling (no GDAL, rasterio or geotiff dependency), and there is no published constituency-level figure anywhere against which a from-scratch aggregation could be sanity-checked. Building one under this review's time and tooling constraints would risk producing exactly the kind of unverifiable computed figure the Atlas's anti-fabrication standard exists to prevent, so it was not attempted; it remains a legitimate, well-scoped future workstream (see refresh_trigger).
decisions.refresh_trigger: KNBS publishes a direct current-290 constituency population table (including a public release of the previously-unpublished 'Volume V' constituency/ward tabulation), or an authoritative 2019 administrative-unit to 2012-01 constituency crosswalk; or the Atlas acquires GIS/raster tooling and constructs a disclosed, independently-checkable S5 modelled estimate from a gridded population product (e.g. WorldPop) aggregated to the Atlas's existing current-boundary constituency geometry.

decisions.reason: KNBS's 2019 KPHC publication does not publish average household size as a direct current-290-constituency table. County/sub-county values are not inherited, and lower administrative-unit household counts are not aggregated without an authoritative constituency crosswalk; the older KNBS constituency table predates the current 2012-01 constituency configuration.
decisions.refresh_trigger: KNBS publishes a direct current-290 constituency household-size table or an authoritative 2019 administrative-unit to 2012-01 constituency crosswalk.
